headline: US tech surged last night with NASDAQ up 3% and gold hitting record highs, while today the ASX gave your emerging markets ETF a big +3.35% boost — but oil's sharp 4% drop dragged FUEL.AX lower as a US-Iran deal rattles energy markets.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Best mover in today's ASX session, up 3.35%. Emerging market stocks got a broad lift, likely driven by positive risk sentiment flowing through from Wall Street's strong session last night and a slightly firmer Aussie dollar making international assets more attractive.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Up 2.58% today on the ASX, riding the coattails of the big NASDAQ rally last night where tech stocks surged. AI-focused holdings like GOOGL and MSFT were among the leaders, and that enthusiasm flows through into this ETF.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose 2.5% in last night's US session to $367.11, as the broader NASDAQ ripped 3% higher. News flow was quiet for Alphabet specifically — this was a broad tech rally lifting all boats.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft climbed 2.31% to $399.76 last night. The broader NASDAQ rally drove the move. Worth noting there's an active class action lawsuit over AI-linked stock losses, but it doesn't appear to have dented sentiment so far.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two rose 2.12% to $216.23 last night. GTA 6 news is keeping sentiment warm — multiple sources, including a well-known leaker, are saying the November release date is still on track, which is reassuring for the stock.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG closed up 1.34% today at $77.22. As a diversified fund with heavy global equities exposure, it naturally tracks the positive mood from Wall Street's big night — US and international shares both had a good run.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 1.09% today to $525.31. This ETF mirrors the US share market, so it tracks the S&P 500's +1.65% gain from last night. A solid, steady day.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dipped a small 0.61% to $6.48 today. There's actually a fair bit of positive commentary around a lithium sector rebound and Pilbara's new processing facility, but the price hasn't moved much — the lithium price recovery is still tentative and investors remain cautious.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL fell 1.85% today to $8.47 — the worst performer in your portfolio. The culprit is a reported US-Iran peace deal breakthrough, which has sent crude oil tumbling over 4% to $81.30. More Iranian oil potentially flowing into markets means lower prices, and that hurts global energy company earnings.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil down 4%+ on US-Iran deal — energy ETF under pressure
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped from $84.88 to $81.30 last night — a 4.22% fall — after reports of a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough that could bring more Iranian oil supply back to global markets. FUEL.AX already fell 1.85% today and could stay under pressure if the deal firms up. Consider whether you want to hold or trim your energy exposure.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision this week — all four big banks say hold
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank meets this week and all four major Australian banks (CBA, NAB, ANZ, Westpac) are forecasting rates will stay on hold. However, the AFR is warning the market may be wrong to assume the RBA is done cutting — a 'prolonged pause' is possible, and one analyst reckons further hikes aren't off the table. This matters for your mortgage, consumer spending, and growth-oriented ASX holdings.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 November release still on track — hold with confidence
watch_today.detail: Multiple sources including a credible insider have pushed back on rumours of a 2027 delay for GTA 6, affirming the November 2026 release date. This is the key catalyst for Take-Two's share price — the stock is currently sitting at $216.23, still down about 6.7% from your cost base, but a successful launch could change that quickly.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium rebound building — watch for follow-through
watch_today.detail: Multiple analyst pieces today point to a lithium sector recovery building around Pilbara Minerals, with the company's new processing facility recently commissioned. The stock is only down 0.61% today but remains 3.86% below your cost base. The recovery story is real but still early — worth watching for a sustained price move before adding.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF riding a strong tailwind — looking good
watch_today.detail: GXAI.AX jumped 2.58% today, and the broader AI story remains red hot with NASDAQ up 3% last night. Chinese AI firm Zhipu AI's stock rocketed after launching its new GLM-5.2 model, showing the AI trade is global. GXAI is still 6.15% below your cost base, but momentum is firmly in the right direction.

watch_today.title: Gold hit a fresh record high last night — defensive assets surging
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped 2.87% to $4,335 per ounce last night. That's a significant move and suggests some investors are hedging despite the tech rally — possibly around geopolitical uncertainty (the Iran deal, etc.). You don't hold gold directly, but it's worth knowing the macro mood is a mix of risk-on tech optimism and risk-off safe haven demand.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street was a cracker — the NASDAQ jumped 3.07% and the S&P 500 gained 1.65%, driven by broad tech strength. Gold surged to a record $4,335/oz. The big story dragging on commodities was oil, which fell 4.22% to $81.30 after reports of a US-Iran deal breakthrough. The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly to 70.74 US cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available at close today, but individual ASX holdings tracked the positive global mood well.

indicators.note: Big tech rally last night, up 3.07%

indicators.note: Dropped sharply on US-Iran deal reports

indicators.note: Hit fresh record high last night

politics.summary: The dominant story in Australian politics today is the RBA's upcoming rate decision. All four big banks expect rates to stay on hold, but there's a growing debate about whether the Reserve Bank is actually done — some analysts are warning of a prolonged pause or even more hikes ahead.

stories.title: All four big banks agree: RBA to hold rates this week
stories.why_it_matters: CBA, NAB, ANZ and Westpac are all forecasting the Reserve Bank will leave interest rates unchanged at its June meeting this week. For mortgage holders, that means no immediate relief or pain — but it also means the cash rate stays at its current level for now. The decision will be announced mid-week.

stories.title: AFR warns: 'Everyone thinks the RBA is done. They're wrong'
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is running a contrarian take today — arguing the market is too complacent in assuming the RBA's rate-cutting cycle is over. The piece suggests that if inflation proves stickier than expected, the RBA could be forced to pause for longer or even hike again. That would be bad news for property owners and borrowers who are banking on more cuts.

stories.title: Aussies warned rate relief may be 'short-lived'
stories.why_it_matters: Even if the RBA holds this week as expected, economists are warning borrowers not to get too comfortable. The suggestion is that any rate relief Australians have already received may be as good as it gets for a while — with a 'prolonged pause' the most likely scenario for the rest of 2026. Household budgets and consumer spending sentiment could remain under pressure.

ai.summary: The big AI theme today is governance and regulation — there's a wave of news about who gets to make the rules for AI, from the US to the UAE to the UK. On the product side, Chinese AI firm Zhipu AI launched a new model (GLM-5.2) and saw its stock rocket, showing the global AI race is very much alive.

stories.title: Americans strongly back AI regulation — new survey
stories.why_it_matters: A new survey published today shows strong majority support among Americans for government oversight of AI systems. This is significant because the US has so far taken a lighter regulatory touch compared to Europe — if public pressure builds, it could lead to laws that affect how companies like Google and Microsoft deploy their AI products, which matters for your GOOG and MSFT holdings.

stories.title: UAE launches Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data
stories.why_it_matters: The UAE has formally established a new Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data — making it one of the first countries in the world to have a dedicated national AI regulator at the federal government level. This signals that global governments are accelerating their moves to control and shape AI development, which will create both compliance costs and competitive dynamics for the big US tech players.

stories.title: Chinese AI firm Zhipu AI's stock rockets after launching GLM-5.2 model
stories.why_it_matters: Zhipu AI, a Chinese AI company, saw its stock surge sharply after launching its new GLM-5.2 language model — a direct competitor to GPT-4 and Gemini. This is a reminder that the AI race isn't just a US story; Chinese firms are closing the gap fast. For your GXAI.AX ETF, which holds global AI companies, a broader rising tide in the sector is generally good news.

stories.title: Tyler Cowen: AI regulation is taking a dangerous turn
stories.why_it_matters: Economist Tyler Cowen argues in The Free Press that the current push for AI regulation is moving in a direction that could stifle innovation and entrench existing big players (like Google and Microsoft) at the expense of smaller competitors and startups. The argument is that heavy-handed rules often end up protecting incumbents rather than the public — worth keeping in mind as global regulation accelerates.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 is locked and loaded for this weekend, with your local Titans hosting Penrith at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday arvo. The AFL midseason is generating plenty of chatter too, with top sides getting stronger.

stories.title: Luai's Tigers future in doubt as Eels halves crisis deepens
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports is reporting the Jarome Luai situation at Wests Tigers is looking increasingly complicated, with the club effectively admitting he may not be their long-term answer at halfback. Meanwhile, a shock rise by an emerging player has created a genuine halves dilemma at Parramatta Eels. Both storylines will have big ramifications for the player market heading into the second half of the season.

stories.title: NRL Round 16 team lists: Every club's predicted lineup
stories.why_it_matters: The full team lists for Round 16 are out ahead of this weekend's action. Key local game to watch: Gold Coast Titans vs Penrith Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium, Saturday 5:30pm. Broncos, Eels and Rabbitohs are all on the bye this round.

stories.title: AFL top seed gets even stronger — Crows in a bind, Hawks injury fears
stories.why_it_matters: AFL's ladder leader is reportedly strengthening its position as rivals deal with injury and selection headaches. Adelaide Crows face a genuine selection conundrum heading into the next round, while the Hawks have concerns over key players' fitness. The top seed solidifying their position could have big implications for the finals race.

stories.title: AFL Coaches' votes Round 14: Swans star makes big move, five players get perfect 10s
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL coaches' votes for Round 14 are in, with a Sydney Swans player making a notable jump up the leaderboard and five players earning perfect 10 scores from their coaches. No specific player names were available from the article, but it's shaping up as a competitive Brownlow Medal race.
